Name: AD service accounts discovered, read-only: traditional accounts, MSAs, gMSAs and dMSAs, classified by type and risk with a suggested target
Program G0 — Ready to Plan: the read-only assessment committed
If late (decisions): The program's assessment goes to G0 without the service account picture, and Phase 1 is sized without it

Name: App registrations, owners, credentials and granted permissions inventoried (Privileged Access plan, A0.3)
If late (decisions): The Entra side of the register has no app registration inventory to start from

Name: Entra workload identities added to that inventory: managed identities, federated credentials, consent grants; ownerless and secret-holding apps flagged
AI seed list: the current AI use-case inventory vintage loaded; agentic, purchased and no-ATO entries matched to agent identities and service principals
Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the Chief AI Officer's staff

Name: SQL Server engine, login and LDAP-bind accounts tagged and handed to the Data Platform plan
One non-person identity register: type, host, workload location, risk and candidate target for every identity
Source of record for non-person identities
Options (decisions): The owning workload's record (the system inventory or CMDB entry and the application registration) and, for AI, the AI use-case inventory, with the register keyed to them; a separate identity register kept by the identity team
If late (decisions): The register has nothing to reconcile against, and owners and lifecycle have nothing to hang from

Name: Gate 0 — Non-person identities inventoried
Criteria (gates): Every AD service account, MSA, gMSA and dMSA, every app registration, service principal and managed identity, and every AI use case in the current vintage in one register with type, risk and candidate target; HIGH-risk accounts listed; stale leads confirmed against sign-in logs, not retired on a guess; SQL Server accounts handed to the Data Platform plan

Name: An application owner found for every service account; two human owners on every app registration and service principal; serviceManagementReference set
AI accountability: a federal sponsor mastered in HR, a small sponsoring group, a technical owner who isn't the sponsor, and a matching inventory record
Owner or approver: Sponsoring offices, with the identity governance officer

Name: Orphan rule for identities nobody will own
Options (decisions): Disable once the identity governance officer confirms the finding, then 30 days for the office to name an owner or retire it (Book 04's rule, applied at once to agents because they can act); retire at once; keep running on a dated exception
If late (decisions): Unowned accounts can't be disposed of, and Gate 1 can't pass

Name: Unowned identities disabled, not deleted, under the orphan rule; each a retirement candidate with a 30-day claim window
Gate 1 — Every non-person identity owned
Criteria (gates): Every service account has a named application owner; every app registration and service principal has two human owners and a service-management reference; every AI identity has a federal sponsor, a sponsoring group, a technical owner and a matching inventory record; every unowned identity is disabled pending retirement or carries a dated exception

Name: Target set per account from the migration path matrix: app registration, managed identity, gMSA or dMSA, or retirement
Retire, re-platform or keep, account by account
Options (decisions): Retire (unused or unowned); re-platform to a managed identity, a gMSA or dMSA, or an app registration with a federated credential or certificate; keep on Kerberos with an SPN, islanded with an end date the authorizing official accepts
If late (decisions): The conversion waves can't be built, and the program's SPN retirement (P4.6) has no list to work from

Name: Workload ID Premium licensing scope
Options (decisions): License for the single-tenant service principals classified Tier 1 (Book 04's position); license more widely; don't license, and rely on app management policies and owner reviews, with no workload Conditional Access
If late (decisions): Workload Conditional Access can't be created or changed, and privileged service principal reviews aren't available

Name: Conversion waves sequenced: HIGH-risk accounts first (password never expires, over-privileged); rollback recorded per wave
Gate 2 — Every account has a decision
Criteria (gates): Every account in the register has a disposition (retire, re-platform, or keep with an end date) and a target from the matrix; HIGH-risk accounts in the first wave; every kept Kerberos account has an SPN owner; waves and their rollback recorded

Name: Program G1 — Foundation Complete: groups and AUs drift-clean, Conditional Access baseline enforced
If late (decisions): Conversion has no group and policy foundation to land on (Book 02 puts service accounts after group migration)

Name: App management policy: new client secrets and symmetric keys blocked, certificates capped at 180 days for new apps; app instance property lock on owned apps
Wave 1, HIGH-risk accounts: workload identities created (managed identity, then federated credential, then certificate); federated token exchange tested
Wave 1 parallel run: old and new credentials side by side for 30 days, then the legacy accounts disabled
Remaining waves converted, each with its own 30-day parallel run before the legacy account is disabled
Kerberos-only workloads: MSAs upgraded to gMSAs; traditional accounts, IIS application pools and scheduled tasks moved to a gMSA or a dMSA
End dates for legacy authentication and NTLM (program D08)
If late (decisions): Kerberos accounts that stay can't be given end dates, so the islanded list can't be handed to the program

Name: Kerberos accounts that stay: SPN owner and an end date within D08 recorded; the islanded list handed to the program's SPN retirement
Rotation in place: certificates in Key Vault, rotated by the pipeline, raised before expiry and approved by the owner
Gate 3 — Credentials modernized
Criteria (gates): Every HIGH-risk account converted or retired; no account with a password that never expires; new identities authenticate without stored secrets where the host allows, otherwise with a certificate on the rotation schedule; no client secret in production outside a dated exception; legacy accounts disabled after a clean 30-day parallel run with no service disruption; every remaining Kerberos account islanded with an owner and end date

Name: SQL Server's application chain on Entra principals (Data Platform plan, Gate 4)
If late (decisions): The SQL Server accounts handed over in Phase 0 are still on Windows authentication

Name: AD-bound service principal names migrated, retired or islanded (program P4.6)
If late (decisions): The program measures AD authentication for G4 while converted workloads still hold AD credentials

Name: Permission sweep: owners review every grant; broad permissions such as Directory.ReadWrite.All replaced with application-specific roles and scopes
Managed identities' role assignments scoped to the resource and put on the app registrations' review cadence
Non-human privileged identities owned, off secrets, over-consented apps swept (Privileged Access plan, A3.4)
If late (decisions): Privileged service principals are outside this plan's sweep, so the least-privilege gate can't pass

Name: First quarterly owner review of permissions closed; access reviews for service principals in privileged roles
Gate 4 — Least privilege
Criteria (gates): No service principal holds a broad tenant-wide permission without a recorded justification; managed identities' role assignments scoped to resources; privileged non-human identities closed in the Privileged Access plan; the first quarterly review cycle closed with its findings acted on

Phase: Phase 5 — Conditional Access for workload identities
Name: Scope set: Tier 1 single-tenant service principals assigned directly, never through a group; workload egress ranges named; managed identities and multitenant apps recorded as out of scope

Phase: Phase 5 — Conditional Access for workload identities
Name: CA015 location restriction and CA037 high-risk block in report-only; service principal sign-in logs read

Phase: Phase 5 — Conditional Access for workload identities
Name: Enforce the workload identity policies
Options (decisions): Enforce; extend report-only; enforce with named exclusions, each recorded with its owner and end date
If late (decisions): Tier 1 workloads stay reachable from anywhere with a stolen credential, and Gate 5 can't pass

Phase: Phase 5 — Conditional Access for workload identities
Name: Policies enforced ring by ring; block events alerted to security operations

Phase: Phase 5 — Conditional Access for workload identities
Name: Gate 5 — Workload identities under Conditional Access
Criteria (gates): Every Tier 1 single-tenant service principal assigned directly to the enforced location and risk policies; report-only results reviewed before enforcement; every out-of-scope identity (managed identities, multitenant and SaaS apps) recorded with the control that covers it instead

Name: AI identity capabilities the program builds on in the agency's cloud
Owner or approver: CIO, with the Chief AI Officer
Options (decisions): Agent identities where generally available in the agency's cloud, with GCC's documented subset; service principals and managed identities under the same governance where agent identities aren't available; preview capabilities as watch items
If late (decisions): Agents are created with no decided identity type, and the production handshake can't be defined

Name: Creation closed: Users can create agent blueprints set to No; agent app registrations routed to the blueprint path; consent baseline applied to agents
Production handshake: blueprint, sponsor, consent, Conditional Access coverage and placement confirmed; access through expiring access packages
Agent credentials: managed identity as the blueprint credential, else federation, else a certificate; no secret on a production blueprint
Agent least privilege: access mode chosen first; narrow inheritance, never allAllowed for app roles; no standing privileged role
Mover and leaver automation proven (Identity Lifecycle plan, Gate 4)
If late (decisions): The sponsor's mover and leaver events have no HR-driven workflow to ride on

Name: Sponsorship tasks added to the HR-driven mover and leaver workflows; ten-business-day confirmation; human workflows kept off agents' user accounts
Agent Conditional Access in report-only: block all agent identities except those approved by attribute; block high-risk agents (preview, watch item)
AI drift checks running: agentic system with no governed identity, shadow AI identity, no accountable human, credential added outside the pipeline
Gate 6 — AI identities governed
Criteria (gates): Every AI system in the current inventory vintage classified by kind of identity; every agent identity created through the handshake with a sponsor, a technical owner and a matching inventory record; no production blueprint with a client secret; no AI identity with a standing privileged role; sponsor mover and leaver tasks live; agent block policies in report-only with results reviewed; no open P1 AI drift finding

Name: Register drift scheduled: ownerless, unused or expiring registrations, passwords that never expire, credentials added outside the pipeline
A full review cycle: owners' quarterly permission review, sponsors' attestation, expiry-based recertification of agent access
Provisional target end state: AD retired, or a dated Kerberos island (program D11)
If late (decisions): The gMSA and dMSA reconciliation has no target to reconcile against

Name: gMSAs and dMSAs reconciled with the provisional end state: moved to a workload identity, or listed for the Kerberos island with an end-of-life date
Program G5 — AD Retired
If late (decisions): A workload still running under a gMSA loses its credential when the last domain controller is demoted

Name: Evidence to the ISSO for AC-2, AC-6(5), IA-4, IA-5 and IA-9, and for M-25-21; the annual inventory vintage comparison scheduled
Gate 7 — Steady state
Criteria (gates): Every service account and service principal has an owner and sponsor, a reason and a target; each is retired, re-platformed to a managed identity or gMSA, or a certificate or federated workload identity; none holds a password that never expires and none is orphaned; drift checks and review cycles running; every remaining gMSA and dMSA moved or in the dated Kerberos island
